items.stem: A client sends POST /users without the required email field. Which response best reports this failure to the client?

options.text: Status 200 with a body like {"error": "email is required"}
Status 400 or 422 with a body that names the email field
Status 500 with a body that holds the server stack trace
Status 204 with an empty body, since nothing was created

items.stem: A signed-in user with a valid token sends DELETE /orders/9, an order owned by someone else. The server knows who the user is and refuses the action without hiding the order. Which status fits best?

options.text: 400 Bad Request, because the request was malformed
401 Unauthorized, because the user is not identified
403 Forbidden, because the user lacks permission
409 Conflict, because the order is owned by another

items.stem: RFC 9457 defines a standard JSON format for HTTP API errors, called "problem details". What media type (Content-Type value) should a response carry when its body is in this format?
A client receives 429 Too Many Requests with the header Retry-After: 30. What is the best way for the client to handle this?

options.text: Wait about 30 seconds, then retry the same request
Retry at once, because the same request may now work
Tell the user their input is invalid and ask for edits
Treat it as a permanent failure and never try again

items.stem: An API has many endpoints. Which approach keeps its error responses consistent for client developers?

options.text: Each endpoint picks whatever error JSON suits it best
Send only a status code and always leave the body empty
Put the error text in a header and let bodies vary
Use one shared error body shape on every endpoint

items.stem: In an RFC 9457 problem details object, which member holds the human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence of the problem, such as "Your balance is 30, but the item costs 50"? Give the member name.
